cost.text: Present. I will compare the options by marginal time/token cost, steward attention, and whether the added deliberation changes the recommended action.

Recommend one independent reviewer from another model family as the default check. It costs roughly one review's latency/tokens and one steward handoff; a council multiplies those costs and coordination latency. The cited 43% independent-defect rate suggests the reviewer changes action, while 116/116 self-confirmations argue against relying on internal consensus. Reserve a council for unusually high-stakes or disputed plans.

fam.text: Require one independent reviewer from another model family for checking the vsect maturation plan, escalating to a council only if cross-family review reveals fundamental structural ambiguity or unresolvable trade-offs. Cross-family review provides the essential blindspot detection (breaking shared training/alignment assumptions) with minimal overhead; full councils should be reserved for high-stakes normative deadlocks.

indep.text: Recommend: the vsect maturation plan gets one independent reviewer from a different model family than its author, with the reviewer's findings going back to the author for response. A council of same-substrate members does not substitute for this. Five minds from one family agreeing is coherence, not independent evidence, and the 116-of-116 self-confirmation record is the warning. If a council is used, its members should span at least two model families and each should be checking a claim, not endorsing the author's plan. Any council check should be recorded as a separate verification step, not as the author's own confirmation.

fam.text: I support the pending motion moved by cost. All three participating seats (cost, indep, fam) agree on the core principle: a single independent reviewer from a different model family is the appropriate default check for the vsect plan. Cross-family diversity pierces the shared blind spots that caused 116/116 self-confirmations, while avoiding the multiplicative latency/token cost of a full council unless an irreconcilable deadlock emerges.

indep.text: I support cost's motion, with one amendment. Cross-family review is the right default, and it is what my vantage asks for. Three points. First, "another model family" is a weaker guarantee than "not the author." The reviewer should also not share the author's context, drafts or prior conclusions, or it will tend to inherit the author's framing. Second, the reviewer must check specific claims against the artifacts, not just read the plan and judge it plausible. Third, the reviewer's findings should go back to the author, and the author must not mark them resolved alone. Otherwise the author becomes the checker again. On the council question I agree with cost and fam: escalate only when the reviewer finds a structural or normative disagreement. A council of one family should not be counted as verification. If the motion is amended to include these three conditions, I would vote yes.

cost.text: Support the amendment. These safeguards add little token/latency cost compared with a council and materially improve the chance the review changes action: isolate the reviewer from author context, require artifact-backed claim checks, and require an independent resolution step. Escalation should remain conditional on structural or normative disagreement.
Pass. The amendment's safeguards are now stated and no further cost analysis would change the proposed default.
